questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a Profit and Loss Account?

options.text: To calculate the net profit or loss of a business
To determine the total assets of a business

questions.explanation: The Profit and Loss Account is used to calculate the net profit or loss by subtracting expenses from gross profit.

distractorRationale.b: This is the purpose of the balance sheet, not the Profit and Loss Account.
distractorRationale.c: Cash transactions are recorded in the cash book, not the Profit and Loss Account.

questions.stem: How does an omitted accrual affect the net profit?

options.text: It has no effect on the net profit
It only affects the balance sheet

questions.explanation: An omitted accrual results in understated expenses, which leads to an overstated net profit.

distractorRationale.b: The net profit is overstated, not understated, when an accrual is omitted.
distractorRationale.c: Omitted accruals do affect the net profit by overstating it.
distractorRationale.d: Omitted accruals affect both the Profit and Loss Account and the balance sheet.

questions.stem: Explain the difference between capital expenditure and revenue expenditure with examples.
markingGuide: Capital expenditure refers to funds used by a company to acquire, upgrade, and maintain physical assets such as property, industrial buildings, or equipment.
Revenue expenditure refers to the costs that are incurred for the day-to-day running of the business.
Examples of capital expenditure include the purchase of machinery, construction of buildings.
Examples of revenue expenditure include repairs, maintenance, and utility bills.
